newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 3 to 863 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 3 to 863 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 863 as of Friday, up three from the prior week and 158 above the year-ago total of 705, Baker Hughes Inc. said.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by one to 731, while rigs working offshore remained at 106. The number of rigs active in inland waters was up five at 26.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down 14; Oklahoma, which was up eight and California, which was up five.
The Gulf of Mexico had 101 rigs.

A total of 354 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down eight from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was up 12 at 508, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects was down one at one.
There were 166 rigs drilling directionally, 67 drilling horizontally and 630 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was up one at 412 vs. 389 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 168 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Friday, unchanged from last week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 184, was 91.3 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area also remained unchanged at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count was up one at 568 out of a total fleet of 605, making the utilization rate 93.9 percent.
